Figure 1. Diverse functions of fungal PKS, PKS−NRPS, and NRPS−PKS hybrids. (A) Examples of well-studied fungal PKS and PKS−NRPS

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Amino acid derived α-pyrone fungal natural products. (A) Structures and retro-biosynthetic analysis. (B) Candidate gene cluster.
AnATPKS is an NRPS−NRPKS hybrid with domain architecture indicated. AnOMT is an O-methyltransferase.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Heterologous expression of atpks and omt in A. nidulans. (A) HPLC analysis of A. nidulans metabolite proﬁle. (B) Pyrophen biosynthetic
intermediates. (C) Chemical hydrolysis of pyrophen 1 to obtain relevant biosynthetic intermediates.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. HPLC analysis of AnOMT enzymatic reaction product in vitro: (i) substrate 3; (ii) boiled AnOMT + 3 + SAM; (iii) AnOMT + 3 +
SAM; (iv) standard 5; (v) substrate 4; (vi) AnOMT + 4 + SAM; (vii) standard 1. Reactions were stopped after 30 min at room temperature.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Substrate speciﬁcity of the AnATPKS A domain. (A) Substrate proﬁling of the adenylation domain. The A domain exhibits relaxed
substrate speciﬁcity toward substituted phenylalanine analogues. (B) Precursor feeding led to biosynthesis of substituted pyrophen analogues.
Feeding of diﬀerent phenylalanine analogues to A. nidulans transformants led to production of substituted pyrophen analogues (6−11), which were
isolated and structurally characterized. Note that 11 may be racemic, as suggested by the optical rotation data.
